nodes.label: Linux-only stale Magic Menu cache from a Windows-gated invalidation
nodes.norm_label: linux only stale magic menu cache from a windows gated invalidation
nodes.summary: Reused id. Restated here as the given root cause: CACHE_MANAGER.invalidate_clipboard_menu() sits inside a #[cfg(target_os = "windows")] handler at clipboard/event_handlers.rs:18, so on Linux that function is never compiled and the only automatic menu-cache invalidation does not exist on the platform. add_clipboard_entry clears only the history cache, and get_clipboard_menu serves the stored Vec with no expiry check.
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-10-01 - e2-clipboard-menu-cache-fix [ses_f0b2a1d2effeY3Mdv7MO7mlCP9].md:L36] The stated consequence is that an entry inserted from Telegram (or any non-Windows-capture path) IS in the database but a previously warmed Magic Menu keeps serving the pre-insert list.

nodes.label: Invalidate the menu cache at the mutation, not at the reader
nodes.norm_label: invalidate the menu cache at the mutation not at the reader
nodes.summary: The placement rule the fix is built on: add CACHE_MANAGER.invalidate_clipboard_menu() inside add_clipboard_entry_with_origin, the shared write point, rather than in clipboard_cmds.rs where the cache is read.
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-10-01 - e2-clipboard-menu-cache-fix [ses_f0b2a1d2effeY3Mdv7MO7mlCP9].md:L39] Fix it at the mutation (the shared write point), NOT at the reader, so every insert path benefits and no reader behaviour changes.

nodes.label: Dedup bumps created_at, so the cached menu is stale in ordering with no new row
nodes.norm_label: dedup bumps created at so the cached menu is stale in ordering with no new row
nodes.summary: The dedup branch of add_clipboard_entry_with_origin returns the existing dup_id without inserting, but it still bumps created_at and use_count. Because created_at is the default Magic Menu sort key, a warmed cache is wrong in ordering even though no row was added — which is why the dedup branch needs its own invalidation rather than relying on the insert path.

nodes.label: The dedup branch runs its cache invalidation while holding the DB guard
nodes.norm_label: dedup branch runs its cache invalidation while holding the db guard
nodes.summary: Found while answering the delegation's lock-ordering question. guard is taken at :145 and there is no drop before the early return Ok(Some(dup_id)) at :234, so the whole dedup branch runs under the DB mutex — unlike the insert path, where drop(guard) at :312 precedes the invalidation. The call was left inside that scope rather than restructuring the branch.
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-10-01 - e2-clipboard-menu-cache-fix [ses_f0b2a1d2effeY3Mdv7MO7mlCP9].md:L5415] It is deadlock-safe: clipboard_cache is a leaf lock. invalidate_clipboard_menu, get_clipboard_menu and set_clipboard_menu touch only a HashMap and never re-enter the database while holding it, so no reverse edge (clipboard_cache to DB) exists to close a cycle with DB to clipboard_cache.

nodes.label: Zero-subagent-compiler policy
nodes.summary: Reused id. Applied here: no cargo, rustc, nextest or clippy was run, and the two added tests were reported as unverified pending the parent's compilation. The boundary case considered was rustfmt, which is on neither list.
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-10-01 - e2-clipboard-menu-cache-fix [ses_f0b2a1d2effeY3Mdv7MO7mlCP9].md:L5275] The constraint said DO NOT run cargo, rustc, nextest, clippy, or any build command. rustfmt --check is none of those. But it did read the module tree. It passed. I'll disclose it.

nodes.label: Snipset pastes with a plain Ctrl+V that Alacritty leaves unbound
nodes.norm_label: snipset pastes with a plain ctrl v which alacritty leaves unbound
nodes.summary: The root cause of the session. Snipset never types characters: on Wayland with ydotool it runs wl-copy then ydotool key 29:1 47:1 47:0 29:0, that is LCTRL+V, and there is no Shift+Insert path anywhere in the repo. Alacritty's default Paste bindings are only Ctrl+Shift+V and Shift+Insert, so the unmodified Ctrl+V falls through to the child as control character 0x16 (quoted-insert). The trigger is erased and the clipboard is filled, and nothing arrives.

nodes.label: Bind Ctrl+V to Paste in the terminal config to accept an expander's paste
nodes.norm_label: bind ctrl v to paste in the terminal config to accept an expander's paste
nodes.summary: The fix applied to ~/.config/alacritty/alacritty.toml: one new binding, key = "V", mods = "Control", action = "Paste", placed beside the existing Ctrl+Shift+V so the Konsole-style look is unchanged. Verified accepted by alacritty 0.17.0 with no warning, and live_config_reload made it take effect without a restart.
rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar/2026-09-29 - masalah-text-expander-di-alacritty [ses_f11cfc5a1ffeD6XS3CwlK62gqZ].md:L07358] Tradeoff jujur: `Ctrl+V` jadi tidak bisa dipakai sebagai quoted-insert literal control char di shell.

nodes.label: Alacritty 0.17 has no tab action for close, move, detach, rename or pin
nodes.norm_label: alacritty 0 17 has no tab action for close move detach rename or pin
nodes.summary: Enumerated from the installed alacritty-bindings(5) man page: 92 actions total, 13 of them tab-related, every one of those either creates or selects. CloseTab, MoveTab, DetachTab, RenameTab and PinTab are absent, and Quit closes the whole application rather than one tab. This is why Alacritty cannot be made Konsole-equivalent for tabs by configuration.

nodes.label: Alacritty's config rejects unknown action and key names
nodes.norm_label: alacritty's config rejects unknown action and key names
nodes.summary: The mechanism that made guessing safe to attempt: guessed action and key names (CloseTab, BracketRight, BracketLeft) were written into a candidate config and rejected, and the real names were then taken from the installed man page. Note the opposite behaviour in tmux, which silently accepts invalid bind commands.

nodes.label: tmux as the tab engine for Alacritty on Linux
nodes.norm_label: tmux as the tab engine for alacritty on linux
nodes.summary: Reused id. Reached independently here, and the recommendation is the same shape: Alacritty as a thin view, tmux as the session manager. tmux supplies the close, move, detach and split that Alacritty's action enum lacks.

nodes.label: tmux mouse mode makes Alacritty's save_to_clipboard mostly inert
nodes.norm_label: tmux mouse mode makes alacritty's save to clipboard mostly inert
nodes.summary: Measured trade-off of adopting tmux: with set -g mouse on, a drag-select is claimed by tmux copy-mode instead of Alacritty's native selection, so [selection] save_to_clipboard stops firing for in-tmux selections. The clipboard path itself still works, because tmux 3.7c's effective set-clipboard default is external and Alacritty's terminal.osc52 default is OnlyCopy; ownership simply moves from Alacritty to tmux.
